title: Campaign: non-invasive brain measurement, probing with ultrasound
abstract: Subcampaign of 'how can human brain activity be measured without surgery, better than today?'. Scope: Ultrasound sent through the skull and detected as sound: functional ultrasound, Doppler, localization microscopy, and skull acoustics models. 40 papers. Status: bounds. Most papers model skull acoustics and inverse problems in plates and spheres; several find non-identifiability or audit failures of published skull parameter sets. Functional ultrasound through the skull is limited in parietal cortex (coarser than 3T fMRI in most simulated draws), while an endovascular array near a venous sinus may resolve smaller voxels than 7T fMRI within about 1.5-2 cm (minimally invasive).
